newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Livshits urges Russia parliament to approve budget.
newsitem.headline: Livshits urges Russia parliament to approve budget.

text.p: Russian Finance Minister Alexander Livshits on Wednesday urged the upper house of parliament, the Federation Council, to approve the 1997 budget, saying the draft was realistic.

"The budget is realistic because it corresponds to all the realities -- the economy, the reforms, taxes, the country," Livshits told the chamber, where the budget is being debated in the presence of the cabinet.
"On behalf of the government I ask you to support the budget. It will be difficult to fulfill it, but the past six months of work have shown that it is impossible to improve the plan radically."
He said the budget would help keep inflation from rising, reduce yields on government securities and bring about economic growth.
The draft envisages a deficit of 3.5 percent of gross domestic product on revenues of 434.4 trillion roubles and expenditure of 529.8 trillion roubles.
Changes in tax legislation will produce an additional 40 trillion roubles, inlcuding some 20 trillion roubles from the taxation of government securities, Livshits said.
New arrangements for excise on oil and gas and tougher controls of alcohol production would add another 10.7 trillion roubles, he said.
The State Duma lower house of parliament approved the draft at a fourth final reading on January 24. It now passes to the Federation Council for consideration.
It also requires approval by Yeltsin before becoming law.
